groups.name: Biology
pairs: An organism that makes its own food using sunlight.
An animal that gets its energy by eating plants or other animals.
A living thing, like a mushroom or worm, that breaks down dead plants and animals.
All the living and nonliving things in one area, working together.
The natural home where an animal or plant lives.
The tiny building block that all living things are made of.
How plants use sunlight, water and air to make their own food.
An animal that hunts other animals for food.
An animal that is hunted and eaten by another animal.
Shows who eats whom, from plants all the way to the top hunter.
Yellow powder that flowers share so they can make seeds.
When a seed starts to sprout and grow.
A warm-blooded animal with hair or fur that feeds its babies milk.
A cold-blooded animal with dry, scaly skin, like a snake or a lizard.
When animals travel far each season, like birds flying south.

groups.name: Inventions & Tools
pairs: An educated guess or prediction that can be tested.
A test you carry out to find out whether your guess is right.
Something you notice using your senses, like what you see or hear.
The facts and measurements you collect during an experiment.
What you decide is true after looking at your results.
The one thing you change in an experiment to see what happens.
Facts or results that show whether something is true.
A tool that makes tiny things look much bigger.
A tool that makes faraway things, like stars, look closer.
A tool that measures how hot or cold something is.
A small magnifying glass you hold to look closely at things.
A glass cup with a spout, used to hold and pour liquids in a lab.
Glasses you wear to protect your eyes during an experiment.
A tool that compares or measures how much mass an object has.
A tool for measuring length in inches or centimeters.

groups.name: Numbers & Shapes
pairs: The total distance around the outside edge of a shape.
How much flat space a shape covers.
A shape with three sides and three corners.
A shape with four equal sides and four right angles.
A perfectly round flat shape with no corners.
A shape with six sides, like a cell in a honeycomb.
A 3D shape with six square faces, like a number cube.
A 3D shape that is perfectly round, like a ball.
A corner that makes a perfect L shape.
A number that shows part of a whole, like one half.
A number you can split into two equal groups, like 8.
A number that has one left over when you split it into pairs, like 7.
When one half of a shape is a mirror image of the other half.
A straight line across a circle that passes through its center.

groups.name: Geology & Earth

When water vapor cools and turns back into tiny drops, like on a cold glass.
Water that falls from clouds as rain, snow, sleet or hail.
The usual weather of a place over many years.
A mountain that can erupt with hot melted rock.
When the ground suddenly shakes because rocks move underground.
The remains or print of a plant or animal from long ago, found in rock.
A natural solid such as quartz or salt, found in the earth.
When wind or water slowly carries rock and soil away.
The breaking of rock into smaller pieces by rain, ice and wind.
Sand, mud and pebbles that water carries and drops in layers.
The thin, rocky outer layer of the Earth.
A large ball in space that travels around a star, like Earth or Mars.
The curved path one object takes around another in space.
The Sun and all the planets and moons that travel around it.

A force that moves something away from you.
A force that moves something toward you.

How much matter, or stuff, is in an object.

Matter that keeps its own shape, like ice or a rock.
Matter that flows and takes the shape of its container.
Matter that spreads out to fill any space, like air.
An object that pulls iron and steel toward it.
The upward push that helps things float in water.
A quick back-and-forth movement that can make a sound.
A dark shape made when an object blocks light.
